findings.affected_requirement: FR-007, SC-001, plan AD-5, and the durable-store atomic conditional recovery contract
findings.evidence: Transaction creation is now inside CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync, so the explicit Serializable transaction is correctly scoped per attempt and has one SaveChanges/commit. However, every retry reuses the same DbContext and tracked ScanExecution/ScanJobExecution instances after domain transition methods have already mutated their state and StateVersion. A transient SaveChanges or commit failure can therefore begin the next strategy attempt with Pending/Prepared and incremented tracked values even when the transaction rolled back, causing the captured ExpiredLeaseToPending, DueRetryToPending, or PausedToPrepared command to return IntegrityViolation/StaleStateVersion instead of being reapplied. If the commit succeeded but its acknowledgement was lost, the second attempt can likewise return Conflict instead of verifying the already-applied canonical recovery. The PostgreSQL suite enables retries but injects no transient failure into this recovery path, so its 44/44 evidence does not exercise the retry delegate's state-reset or commit-unknown behavior.
findings.correction_outcome: Add public-seam regression coverage that forces the configured execution strategy to retry after recovery entities have been mutated, including a rolled-back transient attempt and an ambiguous commit-success attempt. Each attempt must use freshly rehydrated state, execute the complete Serializable recovery transaction in one strategy delegate with exactly one SaveChanges and commit, and return Applied or mutation-free Replay only after verifying the captured execution/job versions and canonical durable result. Prove no nested transaction, no duplicate externally visible mutation, preserved Conflict and cancellation behavior, and one final StateVersion advance per recovered entity.

summary: REVISE. The canonical-fingerprint correction in DurableScanConcurrencyPostgreSqlTests exactly mirrors production stable IDs and materialization fingerprint construction, and all three injected rollback cases retain zero Document graph rows plus an unchanged Running Scan Job Execution. Prior QR-001, QR-002, QR-003, and QR2-001 remain closed on static inspection and 52/52 independently rerun focused tests passed. Recorded current PostgreSQL 17 evidence passed 44/44 with cleanup, but it does not inject an execution-strategy retry. QR4-001 remains HIGH because the recovery retry delegate reuses already-mutated tracked entities and has no commit-unknown verification, so a transient failure can produce a false Conflict or fail to apply a rolled-back recovery. E2E remains required and must rerun after the production/test correction and fresh convergence/quality acceptance.
